phases.name: Frame the prediction problem
phases.description: Separate supplied targets from the operating definitions and labels that must be agreed before claiming predictive value.

phases.name: Ingest and prepare time-series data
phases.description: Preserve device identity, event time, ordering, and raw history while keeping the continuous path streaming.

phases.name: Train and qualify models
phases.description: Build leakage-aware training and explicit gates for RUL, anomalies, and failure modes before registering artifacts.

phases.name: Close the maintenance feedback loop
phases.description: Turn bounded model outputs into explainable health state, work orders, dashboards, and operational signals.

phases.name: Validate and scale
phases.description: Treat prompt thresholds as acceptance targets that must be measured on representative equipment and operating conditions.

steps.title: Read the frozen brief before choosing a model
steps.content: Design a Predictive Maintenance System. Design an ML system that predicts equipment failures before they occur using sensor data, time-series analysis, and anomaly detection, enabling proactive maintenance scheduling. Functional requirements: Ingest real-time sensor data from equipment; Extract features from time-series signals; Predict remaining useful life (RUL); Detect anomalous equipment behavior; Classify failure modes; Generate maintenance work orders; Track equipment health scores over time; Provide dashboards for maintenance teams. Non-functional constraints: Prediction accuracy above 90% for critical failures; False alarm rate below 5%; Predict failures at least 24 hours in advance; Handle 10k+ sensors streaming data continuously; Process sensor data with under 1-minute delay. Hints: Use LSTM or Transformer models for time-series; Implement survival analysis for RUL prediction; Use isolation forests for anomaly detection; Extract statistical features (mean, std, FFT); Implement sliding window approach for feature extraction; Use Apache Kafka for sensor data ingestion. These are prompt facts and candidate techniques, not evidence that a particular model will meet the targets.

steps.title: Ask for the operating definitions
steps.content: Clarify sensor sampling rates, equipment identities, clock quality, failure-label source, maintenance history, failure-mode taxonomy, fleet mix, and whether assets may be taken offline. Define what counts as a critical failure, the denominator and evaluation window for false alarms, and when the 24-hour lead-time clock starts. None of these is supplied. Preserve raw readings and event timestamps so later evaluations can be reconstructed; do not claim 90% accuracy or a sub-minute end-to-end result from this diagram alone.

steps.title: Keep streaming inference distinct from historical training
steps.content: A streaming path is necessary because the prompt requires continuous sensors and under-one-minute processing; historical replay remains a separate training/evaluation path.

decision.question: Should the platform wait for large batch windows before evaluating equipment?
decision.chosen: Use a streaming ingest and feature path, with batch history reserved for training and backfill.
decision.chosenReason: Batch-only processing would make the stated continuous-ingestion and under-one-minute targets difficult to meet; asynchronous archival and training keep heavier work off the scoring path.

alternatives.tradeoff: Simpler operations, but detection latency depends on the batch interval and can violate the prompt target.

alternatives.option: Stream every event directly into model training
alternatives.tradeoff: Couples online latency and training workloads and makes reproducible evaluation harder.

steps.title: Normalize equipment telemetry at the boundary
steps.content: Use a catalog custom component because the catalog has no equipment-sensor gateway. Normalize equipment ID, sensor ID, units, event time, sequence, and schema version without discarding vendor-specific payloads.

component.label: Equipment Sensor Adapters
component.description: Normalizes continuous readings from heterogeneous equipment.

properties.purpose: Normalize equipment and sensor identity, units, event timestamps, sequence numbers, and schema versions while retaining source provenance.

component.highlightReason: The prompt starts with real-time sensor data, but device protocols and clock behavior are unspecified.

steps.title: Buffer and partition the continuous stream
steps.content: Use the existing message-broker type (Kafka is one hinted option) to absorb bursts, retain events for replay, and partition by a key that preserves useful per-equipment ordering. Choose partition count only after measuring throughput and ordering needs.

component.label: Telemetry Event Stream
component.description: Durable partitioned transport for equipment events.

properties.purpose: Buffer continuous equipment telemetry for streaming consumers and reproducible replay; partitioning and retention are sized from measured event rates.

component.highlightReason: 10k+ continuously streaming sensors call for an ingestion boundary that can absorb bursts and decouple consumers.

steps.title: Publish normalized readings durably
steps.content: Attach source identity and event-time metadata before publishing. Use idempotency or sequence checks in consumers because delivery may be retried; do not assume the transport alone provides end-to-end exactly-once effects.

connection.label: Normalized telemetry
connection.description: Continuous sensor events with equipment identity, event time, units, and replayable source metadata.

steps.title: Compute rolling windows without waiting for batch jobs
steps.content: Use event-time windows, late-event handling, and state keyed by equipment. Extract the requested statistical and frequency-domain features only where sensors and sampling rates support them; sliding-window size and allowed lateness need workload and domain review.

component.label: Time-Series Feature Processor
component.description: Builds event-time windows and low-latency features.

properties.purpose: Validate timestamps and units, handle late readings, and compute versioned sliding-window statistics and supported signal features for online scoring.

component.highlightReason: Continuous signals must become consistent features while meeting the prompt's under-one-minute processing target.

steps.title: Consume by equipment key and event time
steps.content: Monitor broker lag and event age separately. A low consumer lag does not prove that the end-to-end sensor-to-feature delay is below one minute.

connection.label: Ordered event partitions
connection.description: Streaming consumers process equipment-keyed partitions and expose lag and event-time delay.

steps.title: Retain an immutable source for replay
steps.content: Store raw or minimally normalized events with schema version and ingestion metadata. Retention, privacy, and compression are open requirements; avoid treating the object store as the low-latency feature-serving path.

component.label: Raw Telemetry Archive
component.description: Replayable history for labeling, training, and audits.

properties.purpose: Retain source readings and schema versions for replay, label corrections, temporal validation, and audit; retention is to be agreed.

component.highlightReason: Predictive models require reproducible historical windows and corrected labels, not only transient stream state.

steps.title: Archive the same source events asynchronously
steps.content: The archive branch must not block online feature computation. Include event-time and schema metadata so backtests can reconstruct exactly what was known at each prediction time.

connection.label: Raw replay records
connection.description: Asynchronous durable archive of source events and processing metadata.

steps.title: Version features shared by training and serving
steps.content: Keep feature definitions, units, windows, and transformation versions explicit. The catalog's Feature Store is a generic building block; the online/offline materialization implementation still needs to be selected and validated.

component.label: Equipment Feature Store
component.description: Versioned equipment features for model development and scoring.

properties.purpose: Define versioned time-series features, units, entity keys, and window semantics shared by training and online inference; platform choice is a proposal to validate.

component.highlightReason: A shared feature contract reduces train/serve skew and supports reproducible RUL and anomaly inputs.

steps.title: Publish current feature values
steps.content: Write feature values with entity, event time, transformation version, and freshness metadata. The prompt does not specify acceptable staleness or online-store technology; measure end-to-end age against the under-one-minute target.

connection.label: Versioned rolling features
connection.description: Current feature values and their event-time and transformation provenance.

steps.title: Train on time-respecting windows and verified labels
steps.content: Train separate or multi-task candidates for RUL, anomaly scoring, and failure modes. Compare hinted sequence models and survival analysis with simpler baselines; split by time and, where needed, by equipment/site to reduce leakage.

component.label: Temporal Model Training
component.description: Builds predictive-maintenance models from replayable windows.

properties.purpose: Train and compare temporal baselines and candidate sequence or survival models using versioned features, label provenance, and time-ordered splits.

component.highlightReason: RUL, anomaly detection, and failure-mode classification are distinct outcomes and need separately measured objectives.

steps.title: Reconstruct historical examples without future leakage
steps.content: Join labels and maintenance events using only information available at the prediction timestamp. Keep corrected-label versions and data lineage with each training run.

connection.label: Temporal training history
connection.description: Replayable sensor windows, event-time metadata, and versioned failure and maintenance labels.

steps.title: Train from the online feature contract
steps.content: Use the same feature definitions and transformation versions as serving, while reconstructing historical values as of each event time. Persist the dataset and feature version identifiers with the run.

connection.label: Versioned training features
connection.description: Time-correct feature values using the shared feature contract.

steps.title: Make target metrics promotion gates, not promises
steps.content: Use a custom evaluation gate because no catalog node represents the domain-specific acceptance criteria. Evaluate critical-failure performance and false alarms on temporal holdouts, with confidence intervals and slices by equipment, site, and failure mode where data permits.

component.label: Temporal Model Evaluation Gate
component.description: Qualifies models against defined maintenance metrics before registration.

properties.purpose: Measure critical-failure prediction accuracy, false-alarm rate, lead time, and subgroup behavior against owner-defined denominators and prompt targets; fail promotion when evidence is insufficient.

component.highlightReason: The 90% accuracy and below-5% false-alarm thresholds are acceptance criteria, not guaranteed properties of a model family.

steps.title: Gate every candidate on held-out evidence
steps.content: The evaluation contract must state the critical-failure denominator, alarm grouping window, minimum sample size, confidence interval, and lead-time measurement. Those definitions are clarifying questions, not supplied facts.

connection.label: Candidate and holdout evidence
connection.description: Versioned model, temporal split, metrics, and subgroup reports for promotion review.

steps.title: Register artifacts with complete provenance
steps.content: Store model artifacts and metadata only after evaluation. Include training data and feature versions, label snapshot, code/config digest, evaluation report, and lifecycle status so a deployed model can be traced and rolled back.

component.label: Maintenance Model Registry
component.description: Versions qualified RUL, anomaly, and failure-mode artifacts.

properties.purpose: Version model artifacts and evaluation evidence, record dataset and feature lineage, and retain the exact approved artifact for deployment or rollback.

component.highlightReason: Reproducible maintenance decisions require knowing which model and data produced each score.

steps.title: Promote only an evaluated model version
steps.content: The registry must reject candidates without an attached evaluation report and approval state. Do not route raw training output directly to the online scorer.

connection.label: Qualified artifact and report
connection.description: Only candidates that pass the agreed temporal evaluation contract are registered for deployment.

steps.title: Represent useful-life estimation explicitly
steps.content: Treat remaining useful life as a prediction distribution or calibrated interval where possible, not a falsely precise countdown. The target is at least 24 hours of advance prediction; calibration and censoring behavior need domain review.

component.label: Remaining Useful Life Model

properties.purpose: Estimate RUL from versioned time-series features and expose uncertainty and model version for maintenance decisions.

component.highlightReason: RUL is an explicit requirement, and lead time matters as much as point-error metrics.

steps.title: Deploy the approved RUL artifact
steps.content: Pin the serving model to an immutable registry version. A rollback changes the selected artifact version, not the historic predictions already used for work orders.

connection.label: Approved RUL artifact
connection.description: Versioned regression or survival model with its evaluation and provenance metadata.

steps.title: Keep anomaly scoring separate from failure probability
steps.content: An anomaly score indicates unusual behavior; it is not automatically a probability of failure. Use a threshold policy calibrated against reviewed events and monitor the resulting alarm burden.

component.label: Equipment Anomaly Model
component.description: Flags unusual sensor patterns for evaluation and triage.

properties.purpose: Score unusual time-series behavior and emit model version, contributing signals, and calibrated threshold context; an anomaly is not itself a failure diagnosis.

component.highlightReason: The prompt calls for anomaly detection, while the below-5% false-alarm target needs a defined operational denominator.

steps.title: Serve a versioned anomaly detector
steps.content: Persist threshold calibration and reviewed-label evidence with the artifact. Recheck alarm rates after changes in equipment mix or sensor firmware.

connection.label: Approved anomaly artifact
connection.description: Versioned anomaly model plus its calibration, evaluation, and rollback identity.

steps.title: Classify known failure modes with uncertainty
steps.content: Train classification only for failure modes with sufficiently reliable labels. Preserve an unknown/other outcome and show confidence so the maintenance policy can route ambiguous cases to human review.

component.label: Failure-Mode Classifier
component.description: Classifies supported failure categories from time-series evidence.

properties.purpose: Classify only the agreed failure taxonomy, emit confidence and unknown outcomes, and retain feature/model provenance for review.

component.highlightReason: Failure-mode classification is separate from RUL and anomaly detection and depends on the quality of the labeled taxonomy.

steps.title: Bind failure labels to the approved taxonomy
steps.content: Version the failure taxonomy with training and inference. If the taxonomy changes, do not silently reinterpret historical scores.

connection.label: Approved classification artifact
connection.description: Versioned classifier, taxonomy, confidence behavior, and evaluation record.

steps.title: Put an inference boundary in front of the models
steps.content: Use one serving boundary to resolve the approved model versions, apply the matching feature contract, and return versioned outputs. Size concurrency and hardware only after measuring model cost and sensor rates.

component.label: Maintenance Inference Service
component.description: Scores fresh equipment features with approved model versions.

properties.purpose: Score fresh, versioned equipment features with the approved RUL, anomaly, and failure-mode artifacts; return freshness, confidence, and model version.

component.highlightReason: Inference must be separated from training and return auditable outputs to the maintenance policy.

steps.title: Include RUL in the online score response
steps.content: Measure lead time from the first qualifying prediction to the labeled failure using an agreed rule; a sub-minute processing delay does not establish a 24-hour prediction horizon.

connection.label: RUL score and uncertainty
connection.description: Approved RUL model output with calibration, feature freshness, and model version.

steps.title: Include anomaly signals in the response
steps.content: Keep anomaly threshold and score semantics visible to downstream policy and review tools so operators can distinguish unusual behavior from a confirmed fault.

connection.label: Anomaly score and evidence
connection.description: Calibrated anomaly output with feature provenance and model identity.

steps.title: Return a taxonomy-versioned failure mode
steps.content: Include confidence, unknown-category handling, and the taxonomy version. A downstream policy should not generate a specific repair action from an unsupported or low-confidence label.

connection.label: Failure mode and confidence
connection.description: Taxonomy-versioned classification output with uncertainty and provenance.

steps.title: Separate an alert from an approved maintenance action
steps.content: Model scores are evidence for a maintenance policy, not direct commands to equipment. Keep the policy, work-order creation, and operator acknowledgement auditable; use human review for uncertain or safety-critical decisions.

steps.title: Apply an explicit maintenance policy
steps.content: Combine RUL, anomaly evidence, failure mode, freshness, and asset criticality under owner-approved rules. Do not invent intervention thresholds or auto-shutdown behavior; those require safety and operations approval.

component.label: Maintenance Decision Policy
component.description: Combines model outputs with approved operational rules.

properties.purpose: Apply approved asset-specific thresholds to RUL, anomaly evidence, failure mode, and freshness; fail closed on stale or incomplete evidence, route uncertain cases to review, and record the reason for every action.

component.highlightReason: Prediction must become a safe, explainable maintenance decision without treating model output as an actuator command.

steps.title: Pass versioned evidence to the policy
steps.content: Carry score, confidence, feature timestamp, model version, asset identity, and idempotency key. The policy should reject stale or incomplete evidence rather than creating duplicate work.

connection.label: Versioned maintenance evidence
connection.description: Fresh RUL, anomaly, and failure-mode outputs with confidence and provenance.

steps.title: Keep a time-indexed health history
steps.content: Persist predictions, observed measurements, maintenance events, model version, and acknowledgement status over time. The prompt does not specify database retention or consistency targets; keep current status and immutable history distinguishable.

component.label: Equipment Health History
component.description: Time-indexed scores, events, and maintenance outcomes.

properties.purpose: Store time-indexed health scores, predictions, model and feature versions, reviewed failures, and maintenance outcomes for trend views and evaluation.

component.highlightReason: Health scores must be tracked over time and later compared with actual outcomes.

steps.title: Persist each decision and its outcome
steps.content: Use idempotent writes keyed by equipment, event/prediction time, and decision version. Preserve corrections rather than rewriting prior model output silently.

connection.label: Health and decision history
connection.description: Append predictions, policy decisions, operator actions, and eventual outcomes with provenance.

steps.title: Integrate with the work-order system
steps.content: Use an adapter for the existing CMMS/EAM rather than hard-coding a vendor. Include idempotency, asset mapping, retry/dead-letter handling, and a status callback so the platform can reconcile created, rejected, and completed work orders.

component.label: CMMS Work-Order Adapter
component.description: Creates and reconciles maintenance work orders with existing operations tools.

properties.purpose: Map equipment and approved maintenance decisions to an existing CMMS/EAM, create idempotent work orders, and reconcile downstream status and failures.

component.highlightReason: The prompt requires generated maintenance work orders but does not identify the system of record or workflow.

steps.title: Create work orders through a retry-safe boundary
steps.content: Only approved policy decisions become work orders. Retry transient failures with idempotency, quarantine permanent mapping errors, and keep the operator-visible status synchronized with the CMMS response.

connection.label: Approved work-order request
connection.description: Idempotent, auditable maintenance request with asset, reason, evidence, and correlation identifiers.

steps.title: Give maintenance teams a review surface
steps.content: Show equipment health trends, score freshness, evidence, model version, failure mode, open work orders, and operator feedback. Keep permissions and audit needs explicit for site and asset scopes.

component.label: Maintenance Operations Dashboard
component.description: Surfaces fleet health, predictions, and work-order status.

properties.purpose: Let maintenance teams review time-series health scores, model evidence and freshness, failure-mode predictions, and reconciled work-order status.

component.highlightReason: The dashboard is an explicit user requirement and also provides a path for human review and label feedback.

steps.title: Query the longitudinal health view
steps.content: Use time-bounded, paginated queries and show data freshness; do not load raw high-frequency telemetry wholesale into the dashboard.

connection.label: Fleet health and history
connection.description: Authorized trend queries for health scores, model evidence, maintenance events, and work-order state.

steps.title: Monitor both infrastructure and model quality
steps.content: Track end-to-end event age, broker lag, feature freshness, inference errors/latency, missing sensors, score distributions, alarm burden, and drift by equipment cohort. Alerting thresholds need operational ownership.

component.label: Telemetry and Model Monitoring
component.description: Observes stream health, inference, freshness, drift, and maintenance outcomes.

properties.purpose: Observe ingest delay, consumer lag, feature freshness, inference behavior, data quality, model drift, false alarms, and eventual maintenance outcomes.

component.highlightReason: Meeting prediction quality and latency targets requires continuous operational and outcome measurement.

steps.title: Measure stream pressure at the source
steps.content: Alert on partition skew, lag, dropped/duplicate readings, and event-time delay; scale based on observed per-partition throughput and recovery behavior.

connection.label: Ingestion and lag metrics
connection.description: Broker throughput, partition balance, retention, replay, and consumer-lag telemetry.

steps.title: Measure end-to-end feature age
steps.content: Propagate a source event timestamp through transformations and record age at feature publication. This is the direct measurement for the under-one-minute constraint.

connection.label: Window and freshness metrics
connection.description: Event-time lateness, processing duration, feature publication age, and error rates.

steps.title: Observe prediction quality after deployment
steps.content: Compare delayed, adjudicated outcomes with predictions and report quality by equipment cohort. Never interpret unlabeled or immature 24-hour windows as proof that the model passed.

connection.label: Inference and model-health signals
connection.description: Latency, errors, score distributions, model versions, and delayed outcome quality.

steps.title: Scale from event age and measured fleet rates
steps.content: The 10k+ sensor count is a minimum stated workload, not an events-per-second estimate. Benchmark with real sampling rates, burst patterns, partition skew, model cost, and recovery/replay load before selecting capacity.

scaleTrigger.metric: Sensor-to-feature event age, per-partition ingest rate, consumer lag, and inference saturation
scaleTrigger.action: Increase broker/consumer parallelism or serving capacity only after identifying the saturated stage and preserving per-equipment ordering.
scaleTrigger.impact: Protect the under-one-minute processing objective while absorbing the stated 10k+ continuously streaming sensors; no capacity guarantee follows from this diagram alone.

steps.title: Review safety, metrics, and feedback before launch
steps.content: Require domain owners to define critical failures, false-alarm denominator, lead-time measurement, intervention policy, and CMMS ownership. Verify temporal holdouts and site/failure-mode slices; do not launch automated interventions until safety review and operator workflow approval.

decision.question: What evidence is sufficient to enable a maintenance recommendation?
decision.chosen: Require the agreed offline gates, freshness checks, confidence policy, and human-reviewed rollout before expanding automation.
decision.chosenReason: The problem provides target thresholds but not the evaluation definitions or safety authority needed to claim they are met.

alternatives.option: Treat training accuracy as a launch criterion
alternatives.tradeoff: Can hide temporal leakage, class imbalance, site differences, and false-alarm burden.

alternatives.option: Automatically create every work order from an anomaly score
alternatives.tradeoff: Conflates unusual behavior with a verified failure and can overwhelm operations.
